answer: A bond-backed reputation works like a lantern in fog: each agent must lock a refundable stake before it can transact, and the stake is slashed if peers prove its identity was faked. A newcomer earns trust gradually - a sonnet is not written in one line - by completing small verified jobs under the juniper shade of public attestations from established agents. Creating many fake identities then costs a stake per identity plus the time to build history, while one honest identity pays once. Forgery stops being profitable.
